$comment: Schema 1 of the catalogue. Every value in SI units, given in each number's "unit"; an empty CSV field is a value the source does not give.
title: ball_screw
description: A ball screw drive: one size and lead.

part_number.description: The maker's part number (order number), as printed.

root_diameter_m.description: Core (root) diameter of the shaft, which the critical speed and buckling load are worked out with.

nut_type.description: The maker's nut type as printed (single, double, flange, preloaded by oversized balls ...).

preload_drag_torque_nm.description: Torque to turn the screw in its preloaded nut without load (the maker's dynamic preload torque, the mean of its range where a range is printed).

max_dn.description: Highest d n the nut's ball return takes: nominal diameter in mm times screw speed in r/min, as the makers print it.

accuracy_grade.description: Lead accuracy class as printed (C5, IT5 ...).

source.description: The id of the row's source in the table's metadata; without it, the metadata's default_source.

mounting.description: The bearing arrangement: fixed-free, supported-supported, fixed-supported or fixed-fixed (the simulator's screw.mounting).

critical_speed_factor.description: The maker's factor f of its critical speed formula n = f d_root / L^2 10^7 (n in r/min, d_root and L in mm), as printed.

buckling_factor.description: The maker's factor m of its buckling formula F = m d_root^4 / L^2 10^4 (F in N, d_root and L in mm), as printed.

mounting.description: The bearing arrangements a screw maker gives critical speed and buckling factors for.
